The strongest general refutation is that the calculus requires pleasures and pains to be measured on one cardinal scale and compared across persons, and no such scale exists. Without it the "sum" of happiness is undefined, so the calculus can't guide action even in principle. You didn't include the propositions, so I can't match this to a specific option. If you paste them, I'll pick the one closest to this argument.

CONFIDENCE: 30
